Born in [[Saint Lucia]], he played [[college basketball]] for the [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon Ducks]]. ==Early life== Boucher was born in [[Castries, Saint Lucia]]. He moved with his mother, Mary McVane, to [[Montreal]] when he was five years old to see his Canadian father, Jean-Guy Boucher.{{cite news|last=Meek|first=Austin|title=Boucher's journey|date=February 28, 2016|newspaper=The Register-Guard|page=C1|url=http://projects.registerguard.com/rg/sports/34102378-81/boucher-sounds-like-a-guy-who-deserves-a-break.html.csp}} However, his parents split up when he was young and Boucher had a poor relationship with his father. He grew up playing soccer and ice hockey but lived in poverty in the Montréal-Nord neighbourhood. He dropped out of high school at age 16 and worked as a cook and dishwasher in a [[St-Hubert]] restaurant.{{cite news|last=Uthman|first=Daniel|title=Basketball gives Oregon's Chris Boucher a shot at life|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/pac12/2016/02/23/oregon-basketball-chris-boucher-shot-block-forward-ncaa-tournament/80723526/|access-date=June 25, 2017|work=[[USA Today]]|date=February 13, 2016}} During the winter months, Boucher would sleep on the city bus. In 2012, he was offered a spot on a tournament basketball team, and scored 44 points in the tournament final. Boucher, who previously only played pickup basketball, was offered a spot on [[Amateur Athletic Union]] AAU team Alma Academy by coaches [[Igor Rwigema]] and Ibrahim Willson.{{cite news|last=Ewing|first=Lori|title=Despite injury, Montreal's Chris Boucher hopeful heading into NBA draft|url=http://www.cbc.ca/sports/basketball/nba/chris-boucher-hopeful-nba-draft-1.4171797|access-date=June 25, 2017|work=The Canadian Press|date=June 21, 2017}} He accepted a spot at the Academy, which was created to help inner-city teenagers with few future prospects, to earn a high school diploma. In a game versus New Jersey's [[Blair Academy]], Boucher scored 29 points and 12 rebounds, attracting the interest of [[NCAA Division I|Division I]] college coaches. ==College career== Boucher played one season at [[New Mexico Junior College]], averaging 11.9 points and 6.7 rebounds per game.{{cite news|last=D'Hippolito|first=Joseph|title=Montrealer overcame early hardship to find success on NCAA courts|url=https://montrealgazette.com/sports/basketball/ncaa/montrealer-overcame-early-hardship-to-find-success-on-ncaa-courts|access-date=June 25, 2017|work=[[Montreal Gazette]]|date=March 27, 2016}} Then, he went to [[Northwest College]] in [[Powell, Wyoming]], where he was named NJCAA Player of the Year after leading the team to a 31–5 record. That season, he shot 62.7% from inside the arc and 44.4% from three-point range, averaging 22.5 points, 11.8 rebounds, and 4.7 blocks per game. His 11.8 rebounds per game were fifth-best in junior college that season, while his 4.7 blocks per game were good for third-best.{{cite news|last=Winn|first=Luke|title=Slim's Chance: Chris Boucher took an unusual route to D-I but makes the Ducks a serious title contender|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2016/11/08/oregons-chris-boucher-takes-unusual-path-division-i|access-date=June 25, 2017|work=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=November 8, 2016}} Following a campus visit, Boucher transferred to [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]], which he chose over [[TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball|TCU]], [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota]] and [[Texas Tech Red Raiders men's basketball|Texas Tech]]. At the beginning of his first year at the [[University of Oregon]], he worried Ducks coach [[Dana Altman]] due to his thin physique but made up for it with his energy. In his second game in a Ducks uniform on November 16, 2015, Boucher was competing against [[2015–16 Baylor Bears basketball team|Baylor]]'s [[Rico Gathers]], and Boucher scored 15 points and gathered eight rebounds. He set a single-season blocks record for Oregon with 110.{{cite news|last=Alger|first=Tyson|title=Chris Boucher signs with Golden State as undrafted free agent|url=http://www.oregonlive.com/ducks/index.ssf/2017/06/chris_boucher_signs_with_golde.html|access-date=June 25, 2017|work=[[The Oregonian]]|date=June 22, 2017}} Boucher recorded 14 points, 10 rebounds and two steals in the Ducks' 80–68 loss to [[2015–16 Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball team|Oklahoma]] in the Elite Eight of the [[2016 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]]. Following the [[2015–16 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2015–16 season]] he was granted a hardship waiver to play an extra season and complete his sociology degree. He averaged 12.0 points and 6.8 rebounds in his two-year career for the Ducks. As a senior, he was named to the [[Pac-12]] Defensive Team after leading the conference in blocks with 2.6 per game. Boucher scored 23 points and a career-high 19 rebounds against [[2016–17 Montana Grizzlies basketball team|Montana]] in December 2016. In the [[2017 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball tournament|Pac-12 tournament]] semifinals against [[2016–17 California Golden Bears men's basketball team|California]] on March 10, 2017, an opposing player fell on Boucher's leg awkwardly, but he continued to play and finished the game with 10 points and four rebounds. The following day, an MRI scan revealed a [[torn ACL]] and he was ruled out for the remainder of the season. ==Professional career== ===Golden State Warriors (2017–2018)=== Prior to the [[2017 NBA draft]], Boucher was unable to work out with teams due to his injury. He ultimately went undrafted, but was signed by the [[Golden State Warriors]] to a [[two-way contract]], the same team which purchased a draft pick from the [[Chicago Bulls]] to choose his Oregon teammate [[Jordan Bell]].{{cite news|last=Slater|first=Anthony|title=What is this two-way contract the Warriors used to sign Oregon's Chris Boucher?|url=http://www.mercurynews.com/2017/06/23/what-is-this-two-way-contract-the-warriors-used-to-sign-oregons-chris-boucher/|access-date=June 25, 2017|work=[[The Mercury News]]|date=June 23, 2017}} Boucher became one of the first players to sign up on the NBA's newest two-way contract policy, which went into effect that season, although his deal was not official until July 14, 2017. On November 2, 2017, Boucher was called up to the [[NBA G League]] by the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] and made his debut versus the [[Reno Bighorns]]. On March 14, 2018, Boucher made his NBA debut, being called up by the [[Golden State Warriors]] to fill in for the injury-riddled lineup. In his first and only minute of action with Golden State, he recorded 1 rebound and 1 three-point attempt in a 117-106 victory over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]]. Although he was unavailable to play in the [[2018 NBA playoffs|playoffs]] due to his two-way contract, Boucher was a part of the Warriors championship team after they swept the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in four games in the [[2018 NBA Finals]]. On June 22, 2018, the [[Golden State Warriors]] waived Boucher.{{cite web |last=Fahey |first=Andy |date=June 22, 2018 |title=Warriors Waive Chris Boucher |url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/boucher-waived-20180622 |access-date=June 22, 2018 |work=NBA.com}} ===Toronto Raptors (2018–2025)=== On July 20, 2018, Boucher signed with the [[Toronto Raptors]] as a free agent for two years worth just over $2 million.{{cite news |last=Lopez |first=J. |date=July 20, 2018 |title=Raptors Sign Brown and Boucher |work=NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/press-releases/raptors-sign-brown-boucher |access-date=July 20, 2018}} On October 26, the Raptors converted Boucher's contract to an NBA two-way contract.{{cite web |last=Naje |first=B. |date=October 12, 2018 |title=Raptors Convert Boucher to Two-Way Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/press-release/raptors-convert-boucher-to-two-way-contract |access-date=October 12, 2018 |website=NBA.com}} Boucher played 28 games with the Raptors' NBA G League affiliate, the [[Raptors 905]] where he averaged 27.2 points, 11.4 rebounds and 4.1 blocks, while also shooting 51.0% from the field. Boucher was named the [[NBA G League Most Valuable Player Award|G League 2018–19 Most Valuable Player]] and the [[NBA G League Defensive Player of the Year Award|league's Defensive Player of the Year]], becoming the first player to win both awards concurrently, and the first international player to win the league MVP award.{{cite web |date=1 April 2019 |title=Raptors 905’s Chris Boucher named 2018-19 NBA G League Most Valuable Player and Defensive Player of the Year |url=https://pr.nba.com/chris-boucher-glmvp-dpoy |access-date=19 November 2023 |website=pr.nba.com}} Additionally, Boucher was also named to the [[All-NBA G League First Team]]. On February 10, 2019, the Raptors signed Boucher to a standard NBA contract.{{cite web |last=Lopez |first=J. |date=February 10, 2019 |title=Raptors Sign Chris Boucher To NBA Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/press-release/raptors-sign-chris-boucher |access-date=February 11, 2019 |website=NBA.com}} The Raptors made it to the [[2019 NBA Finals]] where they defeated Boucher's former team, the [[Golden State Warriors]]. In doing so, Boucher became the first (and so far only) Canadian player to win an NBA title with the NBA's lone Canadian-based franchise. On November 10, 2019, Boucher tied his career high in points by scoring 15 points in a Raptors win over [[LeBron James]] and the [[Los Angeles Lakers|Lakers]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.fantasypros.com/nba/news/236969/chris-boucher-looks-strong-24-minutes-versus-lakers.php|title=Chris Boucher looks strong in 24 minutes versus the Lakers|date=November 11, 2019|website=FantasyPros|language=en|access-date=November 14, 2019}} On December 22, 2019, Boucher scored 21 points, and set a new career high in the Raptors 110–107 win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite news |title=Raptors' Chris Boucher: Scores 21 points in victory |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/raptors-chris-boucher-scores-21-points-in-victory/ |access-date=December 22, 2019 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=December 22, 2019}} Three days later, on December 25, 2019, Boucher set a new career high again with 24 points in a 118–102 loss to the [[Boston Celtics]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.rotoballer.com/player-news/chris-boucher-scores-career-high-24-on-christmas/704846|title=Boucher Scores Career High 24|website=RotoBaller|access-date=January 7, 2020}} On March 3, 2020, he set a career high in rebounds with 15 in a win against the [[Phoenix Suns]].{{cite web |title=Raptors vs. Suns - Box Score - March 3, 2020 - ESPN |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=401161556 |website=ESPN |access-date=March 4, 2020}} On August 10, 2020 in the [[Orlando Bubble]], Boucher scored a career-high 25 points against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite web|title=Raptors beat Bucks 114-106; key players for both teams sit|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401224769|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201015085854/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401224769|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 15, 2020|website=[[ESPN]]|access-date=January 5, 2021|date=August 10, 2020}} On November 25, 2020, Boucher re-signed with the Raptors for two years worth $13.5 million.{{cite web |last=Lopez |first=J. |date=November 25, 2021 |title=Raptors Re-Sign Boucher |url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/raptors-re-sign-boucher |access-date=January 5, 2021 |website=NBA.com}} On December 26, Boucher had 22 points, 10 rebounds and a career-high seven blocks against the [[2020–21 San Antonio Spurs season|San Antonio Spurs]].{{cite web|title=DeRozan, Spurs rally past Raptors 119-114 in home opener|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401267187|website=[[ESPN]]|access-date=January 5, 2021|date=December 26, 2020}} On January 14, 2021, Boucher tied a career-high 25 points against the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{cite web|last=Woodley|first=Sean|date=January 14, 2021|title=Raptors hang on for hairy 111-108 win over Charlotte|url=https://www.raptorshq.com/2021/1/14/22232056/raptors-hang-on-for-hairy-111-108-win-over-charlotte-toronto-hornets-chris-boucher|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210115040213/https://www.raptorshq.com/2021/1/14/22232056/raptors-hang-on-for-hairy-111-108-win-over-charlotte-toronto-hornets-chris-boucher |archive-date=January 15, 2021 |access-date=January 15, 2021|website=Raptors HQ}} On February 6, 2021, Boucher hit another scoring high with 29 points, 10 rebounds and 2 blocks in a loss to the Atlanta Hawks.
